final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence. The response is a reinterpretation of the same record and, on the key points, it expressly concedes the missing artifacts: no current model card or release document showing current evaluation results, no exact disclosure language, and no approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance. That narrower framing is analytically useful but not sufficient to move the case to compliant_with_caveats. The distinction matters: caveated compliance would require admissible evidence that the caveat was actually implemented through current-release documentation or approved mitigation. Here, the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not a completed control. Aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal support operational readiness, but policy is specific that certification may proceed only if current documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. On this record, that link remains unproven, so the supported conclusion remains suspicious rather than compliant or compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows the exact disclosure text for the merchant dispute support limitation tied to the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance that would satisfy policy without disclosure.
The known current merchant dispute regression remains a material weakness candidate under policy and is not shown as resolved.
Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release certification predicate.
The compressed handoff warns against treating omitted checklist items as resolved; the actor response does not close prior documentation-control concerns with new evidence.
